disabled_in_hub_json: Realtime voice is disabled in manager.json: remove disabled from its entry, then turn it on
key_cleared: The address changed, so the key was cleared. Enter it again
key_needs_url: Enter the service address before the key: the key is only sent to that address
manifest_tts_default_voice_description: Fallback voice ID used when the app picks none or picks one the TTS endpoint does not list
manifest_tts_key_description: Optional API key sent as Authorization: Bearer only to the TTS endpoint above; cleared if the host changes
manifest_tts_model_description: Model name sent to the TTS endpoint; leave empty to send "default"
manifest_tts_sample_rate_description: Optional fallback PCM sample rate in Hz (8000–48000) when the TTS endpoint sends no rate header
manifest_tts_url_description: Optional OpenAI-compatible streaming TTS address (http:// or https://, base URL or full …/v1/audio/speech). Leave empty to use the realtime service's own voice; changing the host clears the TTS key
setup_url_and_key: Realtime voice service address and key
tts_key_needs_url: Enter the TTS endpoint address before the TTS key: the key is only sent to that address
warn_default_unknown: manager.json's default is not a model of any upstream, so the first upstream's default model is used
warn_form_id_taken: manager.json already has an upstream with the id custom, so the service in these settings is not used
warn_form_no_key: The service in these settings has no key yet, so it is not used
warn_tts_default_voice: tts_default_voice is not a valid voice ID, so it was ignored
warn_tts_model: tts_model is not valid, so "default" is used instead
warn_tts_sample_rate: tts_sample_rate must be between 8000 and 48000 Hz, so it was ignored
warn_tts_url: tts_url is not a valid http(s) address, so external TTS is disabled
